name: Luis Favela
abstract_title: Eliminativism and E-Cognition Make Strange—but Cozy—Bedfellows
abstract: Eliminativism is a controversial position promoted by some scientifically oriented 20th-century analytic philosophers. The basic idea is that concepts that play roles in explaining the natural world ought to refer to real things, and if they do not, then the concept should no longer be employed. This approach can be understood as taking two main forms (Irvine & Sprevak, 2020). field: Philosophy of cognitive science, E-cognition, dynamical systems
notable: Fellow at Research Corporation for Science Advancement; applies complexity science to behavior, cognition, and consciousness
